task.title: A job interview
task.scenario: You are at an interview for a part-time job at a bookshop.
task.prompt: Imagine you are in the interview. Answer the interviewer's questions as fully and honestly as you can.
instructions: Type your answer the way you would say it, in complete sentences.
Answer every question or point. Add reasons and examples when you can.
In this version your answer is typed. Pronunciation is not assessed.
task.main_question: Why do you want to work in our bookshop?
follow_up_questions: Tell me about a time when you worked in a team.
What are your strengths and weaknesses?
How would you deal with an unhappy customer?

optional_elements: extra detail, examples or a personal anecdote
organisation: answer each question or cue point in turn, adding reasons and examples
expected_response.discourse_complexity: One to three paragraphs or a connected multi-sentence turn.
expected_response.linguistic_demand: Connected paragraphs on familiar and some abstract topics; narration, opinion with reasons; range of linkers; basic complex sentences.
expected_response.cognitive_demand: Give a simple reason or purpose; Narrate events in sequence; Plan, advise, suggest

examples.label: Illustrative outline only - not an answer key; many other responses are equally valid

learning_objectives.text: Respond to interview questions with relevant examples and reasons

criteria.name: Relevance and task fulfilment
criteria.description: Whether the response answers the question asked, covers the cue points or situation, and is appropriate to the role and audience.
criteria.successful_performance: Answers relevantly with some detail and reasons; keeps to the situation. Needs to respond to: Why do you want to work in our bookshop? | Tell me about a time when you worked in a team. | What are your strengths and weaknesses? | How would you deal with an unhappy customer?
criteria.weak_performance: Misses cue points or answers only part of a question.
criteria.expected_evidence: Each question or cue point addressed; relevance of content; fit with the situation. Check each question or cue point in turn.

criteria.name: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Range and precision of vocabulary used to talk about the topic.
criteria.successful_performance: Enough vocabulary to discuss familiar topics; attempts paraphrase when a word is missing.
criteria.weak_performance: Repetition; word-choice errors sometimes block meaning.
criteria.expected_evidence: Topic vocabulary; variety; paraphrase; collocation. Expected vocabulary demands: work skills; personal qualities; customer service.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not penalise a correct plain word.

l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Range and accuracy of structures used; typed text may contain writing conventions the learner would not use in speech.
criteria.successful_performance: Mix of simple and complex structures; tenses mostly controlled.
criteria.weak_performance: Limited range; errors in complex sentences.
criteria.expected_evidence: Structures used; error frequency and type. Structures invited by the task: past_simple, present_perfect, conditionals_real.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not penalise spelling or punctuation errors in the typed text; they do not describe spoken grammar.

l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Development of ideas
criteria.description: How far ideas are explained, justified and supported with reasons, examples or comparisons.
criteria.successful_performance: Gives reasons and simple examples; develops answers beyond one sentence.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Judge development relative to the format (a Part 1-style answer is short by design).

criteria.name: Fluency and coherence
criteria.description: How smoothly and logically a response is organised and extended. In the text MVP only the coherence and organisation aspects can be observed; real-time fluency (speed, pauses, hesitation) cannot.
criteria.successful_performance: Keeps going with relevant, connected sentences; uses a range of simple linkers.
criteria.weak_performance: Frequent restarts or listing without links (in typed text: lists, fragments).
criteria.expected_evidence: Length and completeness of responses; order of ideas; discourse markers; (typed text: no timing evidence).
criteria.evaluation_limitations: TEXT MVP: hesitation, speech rate, self-correction and filled pauses cannot be observed. Judge organisation only; never infer 'fluent speech' from typed text.

not_assessed_by_design.name: Pronunciation
not_assessed_by_design.reason: TEXT MVP: no pronunciation score may be assigned. Do not infer pronunciation from spelling. Reserved for the future audio pipeline.

required_demonstrations: Respond to every question or cue point: Why do you want to work in our bookshop? | Tell me about a time when you worked in a team. | What are your strengths and weaknesses? | How would you deal with an unhappy customer?

the cue-card points in any order

target_level_attainment.1: partial: some target-level features, frequent breakdowns
target_level_attainment.2: mostly secure: target-level features present with some lapses

scale.note: Uncalibrated evaluator scale. Do not convert to an IELTS band without separate calibration.

evaluator_output_contract: criterion_scores (with CEFR-band estimate and target-level attainment per criterion)
evidence_quotes (exact spans from the learner response)
evaluation_blueprint.notes: The illustrative outline in expected_response.examples is NOT an answer key. Accept any response that fulfils the task.
text_mvp_limitations: Pronunciation, intonation, stress and rhythm cannot be assessed from typed text: do not assign a pronunciation score.
Fluency in the sense of speech rate, pauses and hesitation cannot be assessed; only organisation and coherence can.
Do not state or imply that this evaluation is a complete assessment of speaking.

policy.observed_error_vs_weakness: A diagnostic category is an OBSERVED error pattern when at least one instance is found in a response. It may be reported as an INFERRED learning weakness only after >= 3 instances in one response set of >= 100 words (or >= 2 responses) and when the error is not explained by task demands (for example a tense the task did not invite).

diagnostics.observed_vs_inferred: An error is OBSERVED when an instance appears in the response. It may be recorded as an INFERRED weakness only under the policy in diagnostics.policy (repeated instances, enough text, and not explained by task demands).
